title: Create draft bid with no company_uuid
preconditions: Authenticated vendor session; a live RFQ stage exists on the latest event group version
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor and resolve the workspace
2. POST /v1/bids sending only trade_request_uuid, omitting company_uuid
3. Read the error envelope and confirm no Bid row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 (Insufficient parameters) from the company_id.blank? guard in Api::V1::BidsController#create. No bids row inserted, no bid_trade_products rows.
rationale: company_id is the tenant scoping key for the whole bid; if it can be omitted the draft bid is created unattributed and later ranking/awarding queries silently mis-scope.

title: Create draft bid for a company outside the event audience
preconditions: Authenticated vendor session; company_uuid belongs to a company that is NOT in the trade request audience (restricted event)
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. POST /v1/bids with a company_uuid outside the audience list of the event
3. Assert the refusal and that trade_request.bids count is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 782 (Bid could not be placed) raised by allowed_to_bid? in BidsControllerHelper, which resolves audiences from trade_request.audiences.visible for restricted events. No bids row created.
rationale: Audience membership is the only thing separating an invited vendor from an arbitrary tenant; a hole here leaks the event and pollutes the commercial comparison with an uninvited bidder.

title: Create draft bid on a stale (non-latest) event group version
preconditions: Event group has been re-versioned so trade_request.event_group.latest? is false
steps: 1. Authenticate as the invited vendor
2. POST /v1/bids referencing the trade request that hangs off the superseded event group version
3. Confirm the refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101 (You are not allowed to perform this action) from the !trade_request.event_group.latest? guard in Api::V1::BidsController#create. No bids row created against the stale version.
rationale: Bids written against a superseded event group version are invisible to the awarding proposal built from the latest version, producing vendors who believe they quoted but never appear in QCS.

title: Vendor quotes commercially without participating in the technical stage
preconditions: Event group has an RFP technical stage; the vendor has no active TemplateResponse on that stage and is not in the RFQ audience
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor that skipped the RFP stage
2. POST /v1/bids against the commercial RFQ stage of the same event group
3. Confirm refusal and that no draft bid exists for that company on the RFQ
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 737 (You cannot quote for this item because you didn't participate in the technical stage) from check_participation_in_technical_and_commercial_stage. No bids row created.
rationale: This is the code-level expression of the business rule that only technically accepted vendors reach commercial comparison; if it regresses, unqualified vendors surface in QCS and can be awarded.

title: Create draft bid with an SQL/script injection payload in currency_preference
preconditions: Authenticated vendor session on a live RFQ
steps: 1. Authenticate as the invited vendor
2. POST /v1/bids with a hostile string where a currency code hash is expected
3. Assert the response is a handled 4xx and the server does not return 500
expectedResult: No HTTP 5xx. ParamsAuth#sanitize_input_params strips the markup before the controller runs; validate_currency_preference reads params['currency_preference']['code'] and the request must fail closed with a 4xx envelope. bids table intact.
rationale: currency_preference is one of the few free-form nested params on the bid create path and is dereferenced as a hash; a type confusion there is both a crash vector and an injection surface.

title: Submit bid line items for a bid that is no longer in draft
preconditions: A bid already moved out of draft (active or revised) for this vendor on the event
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor that owns the bid
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products with a full inline_components sheet payload
3. Confirm refusal and that bid_trade_products for that bid are unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 32 (Bid not found), because create_bid_trade_products scopes the lookup with Bid.draft.for_company(Current.allowed_companies). No new bid_trade_products rows.
rationale: The draft scope is the only thing preventing a vendor from mutating line items on a bid that has already been ranked or awarded; a widened scope rewrites history after cutoff.

title: Submit bid line items using another tenant's bid uuid
preconditions: {{bidUuid}} resolves to a draft bid owned by a different company than the authenticated vendor
steps: 1. Authenticate as vendor A
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products where the bid belongs to vendor B
3. Confirm refusal and that vendor B's bid_trade_products are untouched
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 32 (Bid not found) from the for_company(Current.allowed_companies) scope, or 101 from Current.user.can_place_bid_for_company. Vendor B's bid_products array is byte-identical afterwards.
rationale: Cross-tenant bid mutation is the highest-value attack on a sourcing platform; the id is an encoded integer so enumeration is cheap and the check must be ownership-based, not obscurity-based.

title: Activate a bid that is already active
preconditions: The vendor already has an active bid on the event; {{bidUuid}} points at it
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with status active
3. Confirm refusal and that no duplicate bid revision chain was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 34 (A bid has already been placed from your team) from the bid.active? && params[:status].in?(['active','draft']) guard in Api::V1::BidsController#update. No new bids row, no change to bid_products statuses.
rationale: A double-activate would create a second ranked bid for the same vendor and corrupt L1 determination; this is exactly the race a retrying mobile client produces.

title: Submit two bid activations concurrently for the same vendor and event
preconditions: A draft bid exists for the vendor; the Rails cache lock key t<trade_request_id>_c<company_id> is free
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. Fire two PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} activations within the 3-second lock window
3. Assert exactly one succeeds and the other is refused
expectedResult: The losing request returns HTTP 422 with error code 516 (Transaction in Progress) from Api::V1::BidsController#lock_transaction, whose key is built by get_bid_identifier and expires in 3 seconds. Exactly one active bid row exists afterwards.
rationale: Auction endgames are the highest-concurrency moment in the product; without the cache lock two activations interleave and produce duplicate active bids that both enter ranking.

title: Buyer places surrogate bid after the bidding window closed
preconditions: The RFQ stage has passed bid_end_time and is_allowed_to_add_surrogate_bid_post_expiry? is false for the workspace
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer with surrogate bidding rights
2. POST /bids/template_input with a complete surrogate sheet payload on behalf of the vendor
3. Confirm refusal and that trade_request.bids is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 33 (Order not active) from the guard in Api::BidsController#create_bid: !(trade_request.is_running || (is_surrogate_bidding && (is_upcoming_or_running || is_allowed_to_add_surrogate_bid_post_expiry?))). No bids row created.
rationale: Post-close surrogate entry is the classic collusion vector: a buyer inserting a price after seeing every other quote. The time gate must be enforced server side, never by hiding the UI.

title: Vendor calls the buyer-only surrogate bid endpoint
preconditions: Authenticated vendor session; the vendor's company is in the event audience
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor (not the buying workspace)
2. POST /bids/template_input impersonating the surrogate flow
3. Confirm the refusal is an authorization refusal, not a validation one
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101 from allowed_surrogate_bid_placement / is_surrogate_bidding_and_is_allowed?, or a Pundit refusal surfaced as 455 (You are not authorized to perform this action) with HTTP 422 from the authorize Bid call at the top of #template_input. No bids row created.
rationale: Surrogate bidding bypasses the vendor's own price-cap and tick-size context; letting a vendor reach it would let them quote under a buyer's privilege set.

title: Surrogate bid payload keyed under a different company uuid than company_uuid
preconditions: Buyer with surrogate rights on a running RFQ; sheets data keyed by a company uuid that does not match the top-level company_uuid
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /bids/template_input where sheets.inline_components.data is keyed by {{eventGroupUuid}} instead of {{vendorUuid}}
3. Confirm no bid_trade_products were written for either company
expectedResult: HTTP 422. transform_product('trade_products') in TradeTemplateHelper resolves data by params['company_id'] / company_uuid, finds nothing under the mismatched key, and the flow fails with error code 4 (Request not found) or 2. No bid_trade_products rows created for either company id.
rationale: The sheets payload is a nested map keyed by company uuid while authorization is done on the flat company_uuid; a mismatch is exactly how a buyer could file a price under the wrong vendor.

title: Create surrogate technical response for a non RFI/RFP stage
preconditions: {{tradeId}} points at an RFQ or auction stage, not an RFI/RFP
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /template_responses/create_surrogate_response with item_type TradeRequest pointing at the commercial stage
3. Confirm no TemplateResponse row was created for the vendor
expectedResult: HTTP 422. Api::TemplateResponsesController#create_surrogate_response scopes with TradeRequest.where(rfx_mode: [:rfi, :rfp]).find_by_id, so the trade request resolves to nil and create_surrogate_trade_request_response returns an error code (2 / 33). No template_responses row inserted.
rationale: Technical responses filed against a commercial stage would create a phantom qualification record that the awarding TNA check then reads, silently qualifying a vendor who was never evaluated.

title: Quote above the configured ceiling price
preconditions: The trade product has a ceil_price configured for this vendor company; a draft bid exists
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products quoting a landed price strictly above the ceiling
3. Confirm refusal and that no bid_trade_product row was persisted for that line
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 38 (Price cannot be more than the allowed price) returned by validate_bid_product_details, which compares estimated_price against trade_product.ceil_price_for_user after rounding both to the currency precision. No bid_trade_products row saved.
rationale: The ceiling is the buyer's contractual maximum; a bid above it that reaches ranking distorts savings reporting and can be awarded by an approver who trusts the number on screen.

title: Quote below the configured floor price
preconditions: The trade product has a floor_price configured for this vendor company; a draft bid exists
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products quoting a landed price strictly below the floor
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 41 (Price cannot be less than the allowed price) from the floor_price_for_user branch of validate_bid_product_details. No bid_trade_products row saved.
rationale: Floor price protects forward auctions and reverse auctions with a reserve; an under-floor quote wins ranking and then fails at contracting, wasting the whole event.

title: Revise a bid by less than the configured tick size
preconditions: The trade product has tick_size configured; the vendor has a previous active bid and a parent bid product
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor with an existing active bid
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products with a price that differs from the parent bid product by a non-zero amount smaller than the tick size
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 214 (Quoted price difference must be greater than the tick size) from validate_bid_product_details, which only fires when price_difference is non-zero and strictly below tick_size. No revised bid_trade_products row saved.
rationale: Tick size stops penny-shaving bots from spamming micro-decrements at the auction close; the non-zero exclusion also means an unchanged price must still be accepted, so the boundary has two sides.

title: Quote above the PR budget tolerance limit
preconditions: The line item is mapped to a PurchaseRequestItem carrying a reference price; the workspace has bid_tolerance_reference_key and a budget tolerance percentage configured
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products quoting a price above reference_price * (1 + tolerance/100)
3. Confirm refusal names the budget tolerance
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 889 (Bid price exceeds the budget tolerance limit) from exceeds_budget_tolerance? in TradeControllerHelper, which computes reference_price + reference_price * budget_tolerance_limit / 100 against the bid landed price. No bid_trade_products row saved.
rationale: 889 is the only guard tying a quote back to the approved PR budget; when it silently no-ops (blank reference key, zero reference price) over-budget spend reaches award with no second gate.

title: Modify a counter offer on an event that does not allow counter offer modification
preconditions: The trade request is not running and is_counter_offer_modification_applicable? is false
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor holding the counter offer
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products with a revised price after the event stopped running
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 33 (Order not active) returned by is_allowed_to_modify_counter_offer, which is invoked from create_bid_trade_products whenever !trade_request.is_running. No bid_trade_products row created or updated.
rationale: Counter offers are the one legitimate way to change a price after close; the applicability flag is the boundary between negotiation and post-close price editing.

title: Modify a counter offer on a line item with no requested bid trade product
preconditions: Counter offer modification is applicable, but no BidTradeProduct in requested state exists for this company and trade product
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. POST /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}}/create_bid_products for a line item the buyer never counter-offered on
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 508 (Not allowed to bid on this product) from the BidTradeProduct.requested lookup loop in is_allowed_to_modify_counter_offer. No new bid_trade_products row for that trade product.
rationale: A vendor who can attach an unrequested line item to a counter offer effectively re-opens bidding on items the buyer deliberately excluded from negotiation.

title: Accept a counter offer after it has already been rejected
preconditions: The vendor previously PATCHed the bid to rejected; {{bidUuid}} is that rejected bid
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with status active to accept the offer they already rejected
3. Confirm the bid status in the database is still rejected
expectedResult: HTTP 422. validate_bid_update_conditions returns 101 for an 'active' transition unless the caller is the trade request owner, a super admin, or the broker company; a vendor re-activating their own rejected bid fails that check. bids.status stays rejected and bid_products statuses are unchanged.
rationale: Reject then accept is the cleanest way to get a second look at the market: the vendor rejects, watches ranks move, then flips back. The state machine must be one-way per round.

title: Re-accept an offer round that was already accepted
preconditions: Knockout or dutch auction; the vendor's vpc company id is already present in current_round.accepted_participant_ids
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor who already accepted the round
2. Replay the acceptance for the same accepted_round_no
3. Confirm the duplicate acceptance is refused and accepted_participant_ids is not appended twice
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 459 (You have already accepted this offer, please wait for the next one) from validate_automated_offer_acceptance; for a dutch event a non first-time acceptance instead returns 458. trade_rounds.accepted_participant_ids gains no duplicate entry.
rationale: Round acceptance is idempotent by contract but append-based in storage; a duplicate entry double-counts the vendor and can end the knockout round early.

title: Revoke a bid after it has been accepted on an event where revoke is disabled
preconditions: The event has is_revoke_bid_allowed? false; the vendor's bid is active/selected
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. PATCH /v1/bids/{{bidUuid}} with status revoke
3. Confirm the bid is still active and bid_products were not flipped to revoked
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101 from validate_bid_update_conditions, which returns 101 unless trade_request.is_revoke_bid_allowed? and the caller is bid.user. update_bid_trade_product_statuses must not run, so bid_products keep their prior status and quote_status is not set to revoked.
rationale: Revoke after acceptance is a withdrawal from a commitment; it moves quantity back into the pool and can silently orphan an in-flight award approval if it is allowed to slip through.

title: Score a vendor with no form in the payload
preconditions: RFP technical stage whose bid_end_time has passed; the caller is a valid evaluator
steps: 1. Authenticate as the evaluator
2. POST /evaluations with company_uuid but no form object
3. Confirm no evaluations row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 (Insufficient parameters) set by Evaluations::ValidateService#validate_params, since valid_params? requires company_id, form and valid_form? together. No evaluations row inserted.
rationale: The evaluation payload is the input to QCS weighting; a missing form silently scoring as nil would shift every weighted total in the event.

title: Score with a form id that is a string rather than an integer
preconditions: RFP stage past bid_end_time; the caller is an assigned evaluator on form id 10
steps: 1. Authenticate as the evaluator
2. POST /evaluations with form.id sent as a string
3. Confirm the type check refuses it
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2, because valid_form? asserts form[:id].instance_of?(Integer) before the in? check against get_allowed_forms_for_user(...).pluck(:id). No evaluations row inserted.
rationale: The Integer type assertion is what prevents '10abc'.to_i style coercion from matching an unrelated allowed form id; a loosened check turns a type bug into an authorization bug.

title: Score with a value outside the event's configured score labels
preconditions: RFP stage past bid_end_time; event group get_evaluation_score_vs_label defines a bounded key set that excludes 99
steps: 1. Authenticate as the evaluator
2. POST /evaluations with form.score set to 99
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2, from the form[:score].in?(trade_request.event_group.get_evaluation_score_vs_label.keys) branch of valid_form?. No evaluations row inserted.
rationale: An out-of-range score is not merely bad data: TNA and Regret are themselves score values, so an unbounded score field lets an evaluator invent a disqualification state that awarding then reads.

title: Score zero without supplying a remark
preconditions: RFP stage past bid_end_time; the event is not vendor onboarding v2; score 0 is a configured label key
steps: 1. Authenticate as the evaluator
2. POST /evaluations with form.score 0 and no remark
3. Confirm refusal, then confirm the same payload with a remark is accepted
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2, from valid_form?: when is_valid_form && form[:score].zero? && !is_vendor_onboarding_v2 the form is only valid if form[:remark].present?. No evaluations row inserted.
rationale: A zero score is the strongest negative an evaluator can give and is audit-visible to the vendor; the mandatory justification is a compliance control, not a UI nicety.

title: Score a stage the caller is not an assigned evaluator for
preconditions: RFP stage past bid_end_time; the caller has workspace access but is absent from the trade request and EGLITM evaluator access lists
steps: 1. Authenticate as a buyer-side user who is not on the evaluator access list
2. POST /evaluations with an otherwise valid form and score
3. Confirm the refusal is the evaluator check, not the params check
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101, set by Evaluations::ValidateService#validate_evaluator via allowed_to_evaluate_participant? -> valid_evaluator?, which requires AccessLists::QueryService(...).allowed?(access_type: :evaluator) on the trade request, the Form, or the EGLITM. No evaluations row inserted.
rationale: Evaluator assignment is the segregation-of-duties control in a tender; anyone who can score can move a vendor to TNA and eliminate a competitor without ever touching price.

title: Evaluate a vendor with no active template response on the stage
preconditions: RFP stage past bid_end_time; the target company never submitted (or had withdrawn) its technical response
steps: 1. Authenticate as an assigned evaluator
2. POST /evaluations for a company with no active TemplateResponse on the stage
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101, from allowed_to_evaluate_participant? which requires trade_request.template_responses.active.exists?(company_id: evaluated_company_id). No evaluations row inserted, so the vendor never acquires a vendor-level evaluation score.
rationale: Scoring a non-responding vendor manufactures a qualification record; because vendor_evaluation_score later drives the TNA award block, a phantom score can both qualify and disqualify.

title: Award a vendor whose evaluation score equals the configured TNA score
preconditions: restrict_awarding_for_tna_vendors is enabled; the event group defines a tna score key; the commercial stage does not allow_tna_vendors_to_bid?; the vendor carries that score; a draft proposal exists
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer who created the draft proposal
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response awarding the TNA vendor
3. Confirm the refusal and that responses_hash still has no entry for this vendor
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 1137 (You cannot award to this vendor as this vendor is marked as TNA) from validate_tna_for_awarding via AWARDING_BLOCKED_SCORE_ERROR_CODES[:vendor]['tna']. proposals.responses_hash is unchanged.
rationale: TNA means technically not acceptable; awarding one is the single most damaging correctness failure in the module because the PO is legally valid once issued.

title: Award a line item that carries the TNA score for the selected vendor
preconditions: restrict_awarding_for_tna_vendors enabled; the vendor is acceptable overall but one selected EGLI has a TNA line item score for that vendor
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response including the TNA-scored line item in egli_uuids
3. Confirm the refusal identifies a line-item level block
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 1135 (One or more selected line items cannot be awarded as they have been marked as TNA) from AWARDING_BLOCKED_SCORE_ERROR_CODES[:line_item]['tna']. No vendor entry added to proposals.responses_hash.
rationale: Line-item TNA is easy to lose in a multi-line award because the vendor-level check passes first; a partial regression here awards a rejected make while the overall vendor looks clean.

title: Award a vendor scored Regret
preconditions: restrict_awarding_for_tna_vendors enabled; the event group defines a regret score key and the vendor carries it
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response awarding the regretted vendor
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 1134 (You cannot award to this vendor as this vendor is marked as Regret). Unlike TNA, get_blocked_evaluation_scores registers regret regardless of allow_tna_vendors_to_bid?, so no stage config can unblock it. responses_hash unchanged.
rationale: Regret is unconditional while TNA is conditional on the stage flag; a senior tester separates the two because a single shared code path would let a stage flag accidentally unblock regret.

title: Submit evaluations while the technical stage is still running
preconditions: RFP stage with bid_end_time still in the future; the caller is an evaluator with draft evaluations
steps: 1. Authenticate as the evaluator
2. POST /evaluations/submit before the stage closes
3. Confirm no proposal was created and evaluations stay in their prior status
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 33 (Order not active) from the trade_request.bid_end_time > Time.now guard in Api::EvaluationsController#submit. No proposals row created by create_proposal_for_evaluations and no evaluation status transition.
rationale: Publishing technical scores before close reveals the qualification outcome while vendors can still revise; the time gate is the confidentiality boundary of a two-envelope tender.

title: Submit evaluations from a workspace that does not own the trade request
preconditions: The stage is closed; the authenticated user's allowed companies exclude trade_request.company_id
steps: 1. Authenticate as a user from a different buying workspace
2. POST /evaluations/submit for the foreign trade request
3. Confirm the refusal and that no evaluation status changed
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 33 when the tenant-scoped TradeRequest.active.rfi_or_rfp.find_by(id:, company_id: Current.workspace.id) misses, or 101 from the Current.allowed_companies.include?(trade_request.company_id) guard. No evaluations updated, no proposal created.
rationale: The lookup is already tenant-scoped, so this test pins that the scoping stays on find_by and is never relaxed to find_by_id during a refactor.

title: Submit evaluations when the evaluator has scored nothing
preconditions: The stage is closed; the caller is a valid evaluator but has zero evaluations in active, draft or peer_review status
steps: 1. Authenticate as an evaluator who has not scored anyone
2. POST /evaluations/submit
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 571 (Please, evaluate on all fields) from the evaluations.blank? guard in Api::EvaluationsController#submit. No proposal row created.
rationale: An empty submission would close the evaluation stage with no scores, letting the QCS report render weighted totals from nothing and pass the event to commercial comparison unqualified.

title: Double-submit evaluations inside the three second lock window
preconditions: Closed RFP stage; the evaluator has complete scores; the cache key eval_submit_t<trade_request_id>_u<user_id> is free
steps: 1. Authenticate as the evaluator
2. Fire two POST /evaluations/submit calls back to back
3. Assert only one proposal is created for the event group
expectedResult: The second request returns HTTP 422 with error code 516 (Transaction in Progress) from the lock_evaluation_submit before_action. Exactly one proposals row exists for the event group afterwards.
rationale: create_proposal_for_evaluations is not idempotent; without the lock a double click produces two proposals for one event and the second one silently blocks awarding with 573.

title: Create an awarding proposal with no event_group_uuid
preconditions: Authenticated buyer with create_proposal rights
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /proposal with an empty body
3. Confirm no proposals row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 (Insufficient parameters) from the event_group.blank? guard in Api::ProposalController#create. No proposals row inserted.
rationale: The proposal is the container that later mints purchase orders; creating one without an event group would produce an award with no auditable source event.

title: Create an awarding proposal on a superseded event group version
preconditions: The referenced event group is no longer the latest version
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /proposal referencing the stale event group version
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101 from the !event_group.latest? guard in Api::ProposalController#create. No proposals row inserted.
rationale: Awarding off a stale version reads stale line item quantities and stale audiences, so quantity reconciliation against the PR silently drifts.

title: Create a proposal while the commercial stage is still in bidding time
preconditions: The latest commercial stage is still running so is_awarding_allowed? returns false
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /proposal for the live event group
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 720 (You are not allowed to award in bidding time) returned by create_proposal in Api::ProposalHelper when is_awarding_allowed? is false. No proposals row inserted.
rationale: Starting awarding mid-auction exposes the buyer's intended allocation while vendors can still revise, which is both a fairness breach and a leak of the comparison state.

title: Create a second proposal while one is already requested or selected
preconditions: A proposal for the same event group and lot is already in requested or selected status
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer
2. POST /proposal for the same event group and lot
3. Confirm refusal and that only the original proposal exists
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 573 (The proposal has already been submitted) from is_any_proposal_in_requested_or_selected? at the top of create_proposal. Proposal count for the event group and lot stays at one.
rationale: Two live proposals on one lot means two competing award decisions and two approval chains; the winner is then decided by whichever job runs last.

title: Add an award response to a proposal that is not in draft
preconditions: {{proposalUuid}} points at a proposal already submitted (status requested or selected)
steps: 1. Authenticate as the buyer who created the proposal
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response
3. Confirm refusal and that responses_hash is byte identical
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 721 (Proposal does not exists) because the lookup is Proposal.preload(:item).find_by(id:, status: :draft, created_by_user_id: Current.user.id). proposals.responses_hash unchanged.
rationale: Editing an allocation after submission changes what approvers already signed off on; the draft scope plus creator scope is the whole integrity story for this endpoint.

title: Add an award response to another user's draft proposal
preconditions: {{proposalUuid}} is a draft proposal created by a different buyer in the same workspace
steps: 1. Authenticate as a buyer who did not create the proposal
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response
3. Confirm refusal and that the owner's allocation is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 721, from the created_by_user_id: Current.user.id condition on the find_by; the Pundit authorize(proposal) call is never reached. responses_hash unchanged.
rationale: Same-workspace does not mean same-authority: awarding is personally attributable and the creator scope is what makes the audit trail meaningful.

title: Add an award response with an empty responses map
preconditions: A draft proposal exists and is owned by the caller
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response with responses set to an empty object
3. Inspect responses_hash and confirm no vendor entry appeared
expectedResult: No HTTP 5xx. add_response_in_proposal iterates responses.keys, so the loop body never executes and save_proposal persists an unchanged allocation; the response is either a 200 ProposalSerializer payload with the same responses_hash or a 422 error envelope. No vendor is added.
rationale: The empty-collection path is where nil-safety bugs hide: vendor_uuids drives every downstream hash build, and a nil dereference here 500s the awarding screen for the whole event.

title: Award with a cross-tenant vendor uuid
preconditions: A draft proposal owned by the caller; {{vendorUuid}} resolves to a company that never participated in this event group
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response naming a foreign vendor company
3. Confirm the vendor does not appear in responses_hash and no PO form can be generated for it
expectedResult: HTTP 422. process_vendor cannot resolve precomputed_data for a company id absent from the line items, so the flow returns an error code (2 / 561 from validate_awarding_quantity reading a blank participant_quantity). No vendor entry is written to responses_hash and proposal.get_vendor_ids does not include the foreign company.
rationale: Vendor uuids are reversible encoded integers; if awarding accepts a non-participant the platform will happily raise a purchase order to a company that never quoted.

title: Two concurrent add_response calls on the same proposal
preconditions: A draft proposal owned by the caller; the cache lock proposal_<proposal_id> is free
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. Fire two add_response calls for different vendors inside the 3 second lock window
3. Assert the loser is refused and the winner's allocation is intact
expectedResult: The second request returns HTTP 422 with error code 516 (Transaction in Progress) from around_lock_transaction in Api::ProposalController, keyed proposal_<params[:id]> with a 3 second expiry. responses_hash reflects exactly one of the two writes, never a merged or truncated hash.
rationale: responses_hash is a read-modify-write JSON blob; without the lock two concurrent awards last-write-wins and one vendor's allocation vanishes with no error anywhere.

title: Submit a proposal with an empty responses_hash
preconditions: A draft proposal owned by the caller whose responses_hash has been cleared (no vendor awarded)
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit
3. Confirm the proposal is still draft
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 683 (Proposal cannot be empty. Please award the vendors again) from the responses_hash.blank? and responses_hash['data'].blank? guards in Api::ProposalController#submit. proposals.status stays draft and no approval_requests row is created.
rationale: Directly mirrors the check_empty_proposal_submission example in the controller spec; an empty submit would start an approval chain that later mints zero purchase orders and leaves the PR quantity stranded.

title: Resubmit an already submitted proposal
preconditions: The proposal has already been submitted once and is now in selected or requested status
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit a second time
3. Confirm only one approval chain and one set of purchase orders exists
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 (Insufficient parameters), because the submit lookup is Proposal.find_by(id:, status: :draft, created_by_user_id: Current.user.id) and the proposal is no longer draft. No second Remark with event_type proposal_submitted, no duplicate PO.
rationale: The proposal spec pins this exact behaviour; a retrying client or a double click must not be able to raise a second purchase order against the same allocation.

title: Submit a proposal with more attachments than the remark limit
preconditions: A draft proposal with a populated responses_hash owned by the caller
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit with an attachments array longer than Remark::MAX_ATTACHMENTS
3. Confirm refusal and that the proposal is still draft
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 472 and the message 'You can attach a maximum of <Remark::MAX_ATTACHMENTS> files. Please remove some attachments and try again.' from the attachments.size guard in #submit. No Remark row created and proposals.status stays draft.
rationale: This guard runs before submit_proposal, so a regression makes it run after: the proposal would be awarded and only then fail on the remark, leaving state half-committed.

title: Vendor attempts to submit a buyer's awarding proposal
preconditions: {{proposalUuid}} is a valid draft proposal in the buying workspace; the caller is authenticated as a vendor
steps: 1. Authenticate as the vendor
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit
3. Confirm the proposal is untouched and no PO was generated
expectedResult: HTTP 401 with error code app_error_auth_failed ('This app is not authorized to use this API') when the vendor app hits the buyer API, matching the proposal controller spec; if the request reaches the action it fails with 2 on the created_by_user_id scope or 455 from the Pundit authorize(proposal) call rendered as HTTP 422. proposals.status stays draft.
rationale: Awarding is strictly buyer-side; the vendor app is a separate client with its own token, so this test pins both the app-level 401 and the policy-level 455 as acceptable refusals but never a 200.

title: Submit a proposal with a hostile object where remarks expects a string
preconditions: A draft proposal owned by the caller
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit with remarks as a nested object containing script and SQL payloads
3. Confirm no 5xx and that any stored remark is sanitised
expectedResult: No HTTP 5xx. ParamsAuth#sanitize_object strips the script markup before the action runs, and #submit converts an ActionController::Parameters remarks value with to_json, so any persisted Remark.message contains escaped, tag-free text and never raw markup.
rationale: remarks is rendered back into the approval timeline for other users, so it is a stored-XSS sink; the params-are-a-hash branch is also a type-confusion crash candidate.

title: Partially award a zero quantity
preconditions: Partial awarding is enabled for the workspace; a draft proposal owned by the caller; the line item has remaining quantity
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response with awarded_quantity 0 for the line item
3. Confirm refusal and that responses_hash has no entry for the vendor
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 561 (You cannot select bid with more than requested quantity). The same guard exists on the non-eRFx path where validate_partial_awarding_for_non_erfx returns 561 for qty <= 0 (proven by bids_controller_helper_spec). No allocation written.
rationale: A zero award is not a no-op: it creates a vendor allocation row with no quantity, which then consumes a PO slot and blocks the remaining quantity from being re-awarded.

title: Partially award a negative quantity
preconditions: Partial awarding enabled; draft proposal owned by the caller
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response with awarded_quantity -5
3. Confirm refusal and that the line item's remaining quantity did not increase
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 561; coerce_awarded_quantity turns the widget hash into -5.0 and the qty <= 0 guard fires. Critically, set_remaining_quantity_for_trade_product must never run, because it subtracts the awarded quantity and a negative would inflate remaining_quantity.
rationale: Negative quantity is the classic ledger-inflation bug: subtracting a negative silently manufactures inventory and lets the same line item be awarded repeatedly.

title: Partially award more than the remaining quantity
preconditions: Partial awarding enabled; the line item has a bounded remaining quantity; draft proposal owned by the caller
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response with awarded_quantity far above the remaining quantity
3. Confirm refusal
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 561, from validate_awarding_quantity (sum_of_quantities + awarded_quantity > egli_quantity when is_partial_awarding_enabled). The non-eRFx twin returns 561 when the per-trade-product total exceeds remaining_quantity.round(6). No allocation written.
rationale: Over-remaining award is how a buyer accidentally commits more spend than the PR authorised; the round(6) comparison also means float drift must not open a silent tolerance.

title: Split award across two vendors whose totals exceed the line item quantity
preconditions: Partial awarding enabled; vendor A already holds an allocation on the line item; the caller now awards vendor B a quantity that pushes the aggregate over the line item quantity
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator with vendor A already allocated
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response allocating vendor B the remainder plus one
3. Confirm refusal and that vendor A's allocation is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 561. validate_over_quantity accumulates sum_of_quantities across every vendor already in proposal.get_egli_vs_vendor_ids before calling validate_awarding_quantity, so the aggregate check fires even though each individual award looks legal. Vendor A's entry in responses_hash is untouched.
rationale: Single-vendor bounds pass trivially; the aggregate across vendors is where multi-source awarding actually breaks, and it is exactly the case the helper spec covers for two BTPs sharing one trade product.

title: Partially award exactly the remaining quantity
preconditions: Partial awarding enabled; the line item's remaining quantity is known; draft proposal owned by the caller
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response with awarded_quantity exactly equal to the remaining quantity
3. Confirm the allocation is accepted and remaining quantity drops to zero
expectedResult: No HTTP 5xx and no error code 561: the guards are strictly greater-than (total > remaining, sum + awarded > egli_quantity), so an exact-equal award is legal. Expect HTTP 200 with the ProposalSerializer payload and the vendor present in responses_hash, or a documented business refusal that is not 561.
rationale: Every over-quantity test is worthless without its inclusive twin; an off-by-one hardening that flips > to >= would block every full award and is only caught here.

title: Partially award a quantity above the linked PR open quantity
preconditions: The line item is mapped to a PurchaseRequestItem; over awarding is enabled with a tolerance percentage; the requested quantity exceeds the PR-level ceiling
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/add_response with awarded_quantity above pr_uncompleted_quantity * (1 + tolerance/100) minus other in-progress events
3. Confirm refusal and that PurchaseRequestItem.quantity_closed is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 561 from the is_over_awarding_allowed && pr_mapping_exists branch of validate_awarding_quantity, which builds pr_level_ceiling from quantity_requested - quantity_closed and subtracts other_events_in_progress. The sibling PR guards must also stay intact: 558 (Quantity should be less than open quantity) and 557 (Purchase request items are not valid) on the PR-to-event and PR-to-PO paths. No PR quantity is consumed.
rationale: This is the only place the award is reconciled against the originating purchase request; if it drifts, the platform over-commits against a budget that a different event already spent.

title: Fetch award approval workflows for a proposal the caller does not own
preconditions: {{proposalUuid}} is a proposal created by another buyer; the caller is not part of the evaluating team
steps: 1. Authenticate as a buyer who did not create the proposal
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/approval_workflows
3. Confirm no approval flow list is disclosed
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 4 (Request not found) from the Proposal.find_by(id:, created_by_user_id: Current.user.id) scope in approval_workflows_for_proposal_create; the route is registered as GET so a POST additionally fails routing. No ApprovalFlowSerializer payload is returned.
rationale: The approval flow list names the approvers and their thresholds; disclosing it to a non-owner tells an attacker exactly which value keeps an award below the approval bar.

title: Submit an award naming an approval_flow_id from another workspace
preconditions: A draft proposal with a populated responses_hash owned by the caller; the supplied approval_flow_id belongs to a different company
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit with a foreign approval_flow_id
3. Confirm no approval_requests row is created against the foreign flow
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with an error envelope from submit_proposal (rendered via render_error_json(error[:code], nil, error[:message])). The proposal must stay draft and no approval_requests row may reference the cross-tenant flow.
rationale: approval_flow_id is caller-supplied and drives who signs off; if it is not re-validated against the proposal's company, a buyer can route their own award to an approver list they control.

title: Submit an award with a malformed step_uuid_vs_user_uuid map
preconditions: A draft proposal with a populated responses_hash owned by the caller; the workspace uses approval flow v2 with per-step approver selection
steps: 1. Authenticate as the proposal creator
2. POST /proposal/{{proposalUuid}}/submit with step_uuid_vs_user_uuid sent as an array instead of a map
3. Confirm no 5xx and that the proposal is still draft
expectedResult: No HTTP 5xx. Api::ProposalController#submit calls params[:step_uuid_vs_user_uuid].to_enum.to_h before authorize, so a non-pair enumerable must be handled as a 4xx error envelope rather than raising TypeError/ArgumentError into a 500. proposals.status stays draft.
rationale: to_enum.to_h on caller-controlled input raises on any shape that is not a pair list; this is an unguarded crash path sitting directly in front of the award commit.
